newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish agency proposes rise in minimum grain price.
newsitem.headline: Polish agency proposes rise in minimum grain price.

text.p: Poland's Agriculture Market Agency (ARR), the food market regulator, has recommended that the government raise the minimum wheat price to 520 zlotys a tonne in 1997 from 400 this year.

The ARR said in a statement it had also proposed an increase in the minimum rye price to 380 zlotys a tonne from 280, and that the minimum price of milk should be increased to 0.58 zlotys a litre next year from 0.50 in 1996.
Minimum prices, which have to be approved by the government, serve as the base for establishing the ARR's intervention prices, which can be up to 20 percent higher than the minimum.
The statement said the government should debate the proposals at an upcoming cabinet meeting on the ARR's annual market intervention programme.
It also said that the 1997 budget draft being debated in parliament included some 85.6 million zlotys for ARR food market intervention next year, up from 80.9 million this year.
